ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the circuit is a port labeled 10 V, with the upper terminal as “+” and the lower terminal as “-”; the upper node is connected by a wire to the top common node, and the arrow of current I points rightward along the top wire toward this node. Between the top node and the bottom node there are two vertical branches: in the middle branch, the upper part is a 4 Ω resistor, and the lower part is a current source labeled 3 A, with an upward current arrow drawn; in the right branch, the upper part is a 4 Ω resistor, and the lower part is a 6 V voltage source, with its upper terminal as “+” and lower terminal as “-”. Reasoning: Take the bottom common node as 0 V. From the polarity of the left 10 V port, it can be known that the voltage of the top common node is +10 V. The voltage of the upper node of the right 6 V power source is +6 V, so the current through the right 4 Ω resistor from top to bottom is (10−6)/4 = 1 A. The direction of the 3 A current source in the middle branch is upward, so counted according to the reference direction of “flowing out from the top node downward,” it is −3 A. Writing KCL for the top node, the left-side current I is equal to the sum of the currents flowing out from the top node downward through the vertical branches: I = 1 + (−3) = −2 A.

method.method_draft: Take the bottom node as 0 V and the top node as +10 V from the labeled 10 V port. In the right branch, the node above the 6 V source is at +6 V, so the current through the 4 Ω resistor from top to bottom is (10−6)/4 = 1 A. In the middle branch, the 3 A current source drives 3 A upward, so relative to downward current leaving the top node it contributes −3 A. Apply KCL at the top node: the current I entering from the left equals the sum of branch currents leaving downward, I = 1 − 3 = −2 A.

method.method_draft: Compute each branch's contribution to the input current with the sign positive in the direction of the I arrow into the network. The middle branch current is fixed by the current source at 3 A upward, meaning 3 A leaves the top node toward the source terminal, so its input-current contribution is −3 A. For the right branch, the 6 V source fixes the lower end of the 4 Ω resistor at +6 V while the port top node is +10 V, so it draws (10−6)/4 = +1 A from the port. Add the parallel branch port currents: I = −3 A + 1 A = −2 A.
